title: Helaman’s letter
summary: Moroni receives Helaman’s letter, which opens with a greeting and says Helaman will report on the warfare in his part of the land.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni received an epistle from Helaman on the second day in the first month of the thirtieth year of the judges’ reign.
The epistle begins with Helaman addressing Moroni and saying he has something to tell him about the warfare in his part of the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni can be shown receiving and reading a letter.
unspecified_visual_details: The room, clothing, letter’s appearance, and whether anyone else is present.

narration.text: Moroni received an epistle from Helaman
concerning our warfare in this part of the land.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Helaman writing or delivering the letter; neither action is stated.

title: The young men volunteer
summary: In the letter, Helaman reports that two thousand young men descended from Laman took up weapons and came to defend their country. Their fathers had covenanted not to take up weapons against their brethren; when the young men were ready to break that covenant to defend the Nephites, Helaman would not let them.

explicit_facts.text: The two thousand young men are descendants of Laman, eldest son of Lehi.
The two thousand young men took up weapons and wanted Helaman to lead them in defending their country.
Their fathers had covenanted not to take up weapons against their brethren to shed blood.
In the twenty-sixth year, the young men were about to break that covenant and take up weapons in the Nephites’ defense.
Helaman would not allow them to break the covenant, supposing God would strengthen the Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The young men can be shown with weapons, expressing readiness to defend their country.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the young men are shown in a single gathering or in separate moments; their clothing and the place of the reported events.

narration.text: two thousand of these young men have taken their weapons of war
I would not suffer them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The covenant and Helaman’s decision are reported in the letter, not narrated as a present-time event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show their fathers making the covenant in this scene.

title: Helaman joins Antipus
summary: Helaman reports marching at the head of the two thousand young men to Judea and joining them to Antipus’s army. Antipus rejoices at the added strength; his army had been reduced by the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: In the twenty-sixth year, Helaman led two thousand young men to the city of Judea to assist Antipus.
Helaman joined the two thousand to Antipus’s army, and Antipus rejoiced at the increased strength.
The Lamanites had reduced Antipus’s army by killing many of their men.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman and the young men can be shown arriving at Judea and joining Antipus’s army.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise arrangement of the army and the appearance of its members.

narration.text: I, Helaman, did march at the head of these two thousand young men
Antipus did rejoice exceedingly

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The young men are called Helaman’s sons figuratively; the text does not say they are his biological children.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier deaths as a present action in this moment.

title: The losses and captured captains
summary: Helaman says the Nephites can console themselves that those who died did so for their country and God. He reports that the Lamanites retained many prisoners, all chief captains, and supposes they were then in the land of Nephi if they had not been slain.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman says the fallen died in the cause of their country and God, and that they are happy.
The Lamanites retained many prisoners, all of whom were chief captains; Helaman supposes they were in the land of Nephi if not slain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: No specific visual action is needed; this can be conveyed as off-screen narration over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and location of the prisoners, and the circumstances of any deaths.

narration.text: they have died in the cause of their country and of their God
the Lamanites had also retained many prisoners

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are reported losses and a supposition about the prisoners’ location, not a new present-time scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the deaths, capture, or prisoners’ present location as witnessed events.

title: Cities taken; Judea fortified
summary: Helaman lists Manti, Zeezrom, Cumeni, and Antiparah as cities taken by the Lamanites. At Judea he found Antipus and his men laboring to fortify the city, exhausted from fighting by day and working by night.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites had obtained possession of Manti, Zeezrom, Cumeni, and Antiparah after many Nephite deaths.
When Helaman arrived at Judea, Antipus and his men were working hard to fortify it.
Antipus’s men were depressed in body and spirit after fighting by day and laboring by night to maintain their cities.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Antipus’s men can be shown working on the city’s defenses while visibly weary.
unspecified_visual_details: The fortifications’ design and the men’s clothing.

narration.text: toiling with their might to fortify the city
depressed in body as well as in spirit

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The four captured cities are listed in narration, not shown as separate present-time events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the cities being captured.

title: A stronger defense
summary: Helaman says the added young men gave Antipus’s determined force hope and joy. The Lamanites, under Ammoron’s orders, did not attack Judea. The Nephites prepared the city and themselves for defense as the twenty-seventh year began.

explicit_facts.text: Antipus’s force was determined to conquer or die, and Helaman’s young men gave them hope and joy.
Ammoron ordered the Lamanites not to attack Judea or the Nephites there; the Nephites were thereby preserved.
At the commencement of the twenty-seventh year, the Nephites had prepared their city and themselves for defense.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The defenders can be shown preparing Judea’s defenses.
unspecified_visual_details: The particular defensive preparations and the location of Ammoron when he gave the order.

narration.text: gave them great hopes and much joy.
we had prepared our city and ourselves for defence.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Helaman attributes their preservation to favor from the Lord; no visible divine appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Ammoron giving his order in person; the text does not specify his location or manner of issuing it.

title: Watchers around Judea
summary: The Nephites wanted the Lamanites to attack them rather than attack the Lamanites in their strongholds. They kept spies watching so the Lamanites could not pass toward the northern cities unnoticed. Helaman explains that the Nephites hoped to attack the Lamanite rear if they passed, but this did not happen.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites wanted the Lamanites to attack Judea and did not want to attack their strongholds.
They kept spies around to watch Lamanite movements and prevent an unnoticed passage toward the other northern cities.
The Nephites hoped to strike the Lamanites from behind if they passed, but were disappointed in this desire.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Spies can be shown keeping watch around Judea.
unspecified_visual_details: The spies’ exact positions, appearance, and what they see.

narration.text: we kept spies out round about
we were disappointed in this our desire.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The proposed rear attack is a plan, not an event that occurred.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the planned attack taking place.

title: The Lamanites hold their cities
summary: The Lamanites did not risk passing Judea with all or part of their army, marching against Zarahemla, or crossing the head of Sidon toward Nephihah. They remained determined to hold the cities they had taken.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites dared not pass Judea with all or part of their army.
They did not march against Zarahemla or cross the head of Sidon to Nephihah.
They were determined to maintain the cities they had taken.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites can be shown holding a position at an unspecified location.
unspecified_visual_details: Which city or position is shown, and the Lamanite army’s arrangement.

narration.text: they were determined to maintain those cities which they had taken.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage reports places the Lamanites did not attack; those rejected routes are not depicted as events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show an attack on Zarahemla or Nephihah.

title: Provisions and reinforcements
summary: In the second month, provisions arrived from the fathers of Helaman’s young men, along with two thousand men sent from Zarahemla. The Nephites were prepared with ten thousand men and provisions for them, their wives, and children.

explicit_facts.text: Provisions were brought from the fathers of Helaman’s two thousand young men.
Two thousand men were sent from Zarahemla; the Nephites had ten thousand men and provisions for them and their wives and children.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Provisions and reinforcements can be shown arriving at Judea.
unspecified_visual_details: The provisions, transport, identities of the fathers, and whether wives and children are present.

narration.text: there was brought unto us many provisions
we were prepared with ten thousand men

prohibited_inventions: Do not assign names or individual biographies to the fathers or reinforcements.

title: The feigned supply march
summary: As Nephite forces and provisions increased, the Lamanites grew fearful and sallied forth to try to stop further support. Antipus ordered Helaman to march with the young men toward a neighboring city as if carrying provisions, near Antiparah and toward a city beyond by the seashore.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites saw Nephite forces and provisions increasing and began to sally forth in an attempt to stop them.
Antipus ordered Helaman to march with the young men as if carrying provisions to a neighboring city.
The route was near Antiparah, as if going to a city beyond in the borders by the seashore.
Helaman and the young men marched out as if carrying provisions to that city.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman’s group can be shown setting out with provisions as part of the feint.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise route, provisions, and appearance of the seashore destination.

narration.text: as if we were carrying provisions
we did march forth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supposed destination is part of the stratagem, not a stated arrival.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the group reaching the neighboring city or seashore.

title: The armies leave Judea
summary: After Helaman’s force came near Antiparah, Antipus marched out with part of his army, leaving the rest to maintain Judea. Antiparah held the Lamanites’ strongest and most numerous army, which came out against Helaman after its spies informed it.

explicit_facts.text: Antipus marched with part of his army only after Helaman’s force had gone out and come near Antiparah, leaving the rest to maintain Judea.
The strongest and most numerous Lamanite army was stationed in Antiparah.
After their spies informed them, the Lamanites came out with their army and marched against Helaman’s force.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanite army can be shown advancing from Antiparah toward Helaman’s force.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the city, the spies’ report, and the armies’ formation.

narration.text: they came forth with their army and marched against us.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the spies’ report as spoken dialogue; the text does not supply its words.

title: The Lamanites pursue north
summary: Helaman’s force fled northward, drawing the Lamanites a considerable distance. When the Lamanites saw Antipus’s army pursuing, they continued straight after Helaman’s force rather than turn aside.
locations: North of the city of Antiparah

explicit_facts.text: Helaman’s force fled northward before the Lamanites and led their most powerful army away.
The Lamanites saw Antipus’s army pursuing and continued straight after Helaman’s force for a considerable distance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two forces can be shown fleeing and pursuing in a straight northward course, with Antipus’s army behind the Lamanites.
unspecified_visual_details: The terrain, distance, and relative size of the forces.

narration.text: we did flee before them, northward.
pursued their march in a straight course after us

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The stated intent to slay Helaman’s force before Antipus could overtake them is Helaman’s supposition.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the inferred intent as spoken or certain.

title: Night halt
summary: Antipus quickened his army’s march when he saw Helaman’s force in danger, but night fell before either pursuing army caught the other. Helaman’s force camped for the night.

explicit_facts.text: Antipus hastened his army’s march when he saw Helaman’s force in danger.
Night prevented Antipus from overtaking either Helaman’s force or the Lamanites; Helaman’s force camped for the night.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman’s force can be shown camped at night while the pursuers remain out of reach.
unspecified_visual_details: The camp’s arrangement, shelter, and whether the other armies are visible from it.

narration.text: therefore we did camp for the night.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show a night battle; none occurred in the account.

title: Flight into the wilderness
summary: Before dawn, the Lamanites pursued Helaman’s force again. Too weak to fight, Helaman continued the march into the wilderness. They fled all day until dark while both sides avoided turning aside.

explicit_facts.text: Before dawn, the Lamanites pursued Helaman’s force; Helaman continued marching because his force was not strong enough to contend with them.
Helaman’s force marched into the wilderness and fled all day until dark; both sides avoided turning aside.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman’s force can be shown continuing its flight through wilderness terrain, with the Lamanites pursuing.
unspecified_visual_details: The wilderness terrain and the precise distance between the forces.

narration.text: we did continue our march
we did flee all that day into the wilderness

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the young men captured or killed; Helaman’s stated concern is not an event.

title: The third day’s pursuit
summary: At morning light the Lamanites were upon Helaman’s force, which fled before them. The Lamanites halted before pursuing far; it was the morning of the third day of the seventh month.

explicit_facts.text: At morning light, Helaman’s force saw the Lamanites upon them and fled before them.
The Lamanites did not pursue far before halting; it was the morning of the third day of the seventh month.

unspecified_visual_details: The distance between the forces and the reason the Lamanites halted.

title: Helaman asks his sons
summary: Helaman tells his men he does not know why the Lamanites halted and asks whether they will go against them in battle, while cautioning that the halt may be a snare.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman did not know whether Antipus had overtaken the Lamanites.
Helaman told his men the Lamanites might have halted to lure them into a snare and asked whether they would go to battle.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman can be shown addressing the young men, with the halted Lamanites at a distance if visible.
unspecified_visual_details: The men’s arrangement and the Lamanites’ visibility from where Helaman speaks.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the possibility of a snare as a confirmed trap.

title: The young men answer
summary: Helaman reports their great courage. The young men say God is with them and ask to go so they can prevent the Lamanites from overpowering Antipus’s army; they say they would not kill their brethren if left alone. Though inexperienced in battle, they did not fear death and recalled their mothers’ teaching and their own trust in it.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman says he had never seen such courage among the Nephites.
The young men say God is with them, ask to go forth, and say they would not kill their brethren if left alone; they urge action lest Antipus’s army be overpowered.
They had never fought, did not fear death, and valued their fathers’ liberty over their own lives; their mothers had taught them that God would deliver them if they did not doubt.
The young men say they do not doubt their mothers knew it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The young men can be shown answering Helaman with courage.
unspecified_visual_details: The mothers’ identities, appearance, and any earlier teaching scene.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The two thousand young men

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The two thousand young men

title: Helaman returns to the battle
summary: Helaman returned with the two thousand against the Lamanites who had pursued them. Antipus’s army had overtaken the Lamanites and a battle was underway; Antipus’s weary army was close to falling into Lamanite hands.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman returned with his two thousand against the Lamanites who had pursued them.
Antipus’s army had overtaken the Lamanites and a terrible battle had commenced.

title: The Lamanites turn

title: The Lamanites surrender
summary: The Nephite forces surrounded and defeated the Lamanites, who surrendered their weapons and themselves as prisoners. Afterward, Helaman counted the young men who had fought with him, fearing many had been slain.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman’s force, the people of Antipus, and the people of Nephi surrounded and defeated the Lamanites, who surrendered their weapons and themselves as prisoners.

title: Prisoners sent away; Helaman returns
summary: Because there was no place to guard the prisoners from the Lamanite armies, Helaman sent them to Zarahemla with some of Antipus’s surviving men. He took the rest of those men, joined them to his stripling Ammonites, and marched back to Judea.
